hot.pointer_line: On now: the Suquet de Peix days in Roses to Sunday 25 October, Girona's Fires de Sant Narcís from 23 October to 1 November, clocks back on 25 October, the castanyada for Tots Sants on 1 November, the olive harvest in the Empordà, the first calçots (Calçofest in Valls, 21 November) and the MICHELIN Spain 2027 gala in Huesca on 24 November; the sea is cooling from about 20C and the urchins wait for January.

groups.title: In the water
groups.desc: The sea is still swimmable on a calm day, the Palamós trawlers are working and the urchins are a winter promise, not yet a plate.

items.name: The sea off Palamós in late October
items.teaser: Around 19-22C through October, cooling toward 18C by mid-November: swim on still days only
items.story: The daily table for Palamós shows October water between roughly 19 and 22C, warmest in the middle of the month and nearer 19 or 20C by the 31st. A mid-November forecast for the same port gave 18C. That is a brisk swim off the Palafrugell coves, fine for a short dip from the tender, not for an afternoon in the water. The tramuntana season is back, and a day of north wind churns the bays and drops the surface temperature. On Sunday 25 October the clocks go back, so the warm part of the day comes earlier.
items.why: Plan any swim for midday after two calm days, in a south-facing cove.
facts: Mid-Oct to end Nov, cooling week by week

items.name: The gamba de Palamós is on the boats
items.teaser: The trawl fleet is working this autumn; its long biological stop comes in winter, not now
items.story: The red prawn is trawled from the deep canyon off Palamós and sold each weekday afternoon at the descending auction on the fishing quay. Under the management plan in force since 2013, the fleet must stop for 52 working days a year, split into two periods. In 2025 the main stop began on 2 January and ran to 16 February; on the first day back, 19 boats landed about 5,700 kg of fish, 554 kg of it gamba. The 2026-27 calendar was not found, but autumn is outside that winter stop, so the prawn is coming in now.
items.why: Watch the afternoon auction from the Espai del Peix, then eat the prawn on the port the same evening.
facts: Weekdays now; winter stoppage expected from early January (2 Jan-16 Feb in 2025)

items.name: The urchins are still out of season
items.teaser: No garoines until the cold months: the closed season is long and the Garoinada starts in January
items.story: The coast's urchin lunches belong to winter. Palafrugell's tourism pages describe the closed season for the garoina as much wider than the few weeks of the restaurant campaign, and catching them out of season, or buying them, can bring fines from 151 to 30,000 EUR. The Catalan press has reported the recreational daily limit being cut from 150 to 75 pieces. The exact 2026-27 opening date was not found online. La Garoinada in Palafrugell ran 16 January to 29 March in 2026 and 17 January to 31 March in 2025; 2027 dates are not out.
items.why: Do not ask for urchins this autumn; book the Garoinada for late January instead.
facts: Out of season now; Garoinada usually mid-Jan to late March

items.name: Fires de Sant Narcís, Girona: 23 Oct-1 Nov
items.teaser: Girona's big autumn fair: ten days of rides on the Devesa, correfoc, castellers and nightly concerts
items.story: Girona keeps its feast for Sant Narcís, the patron saint whose day is 29 October, and builds ten days around it. In 2026 the Fires run from Friday 23 October to Sunday 1 November, with close to 200 events. The fairground fills the Devesa park; the correfoc runs on Saturday 24 at 22:30, the castellers raise towers on Sunday 25 at 11:30, and there are concerts every night at La Copa, opened by Miki Núñez. The fireworks close it on 1 November at 20:00. Expect the old town packed and parking scarce.
items.why: Go for the Sunday-morning castellers and an early lunch in the Barri Vell; leave the correfoc to those who like sparks.

items.name: The olive harvest and the oli nou
items.teaser: The Empordà olives are coming in; the new DOP oil is usually presented in Girona in mid-December
items.story: Late autumn is olive time on the Empordà plain. The DOP Oli de l'Empordà is pressed from the native Argudell, Curivell and Llei de Cadaqués varieties, plus Arbequina, and the first green, peppery oil of the season is the one to taste. The DOP's own presentation of the new oil has been held at the Mercat del Lleó in Girona in mid-December: on 14 December in 2024 and 2019, on 11 December in 2021. The 2026 date was not found. Nationally, first estimates on 1 October pointed to a crop of about 1.6 million tonnes, up 23%.
items.why: Ask at the Empordàlia cooperative shop in Pau whether the oli nou is in yet.
facts: Harvest under way; new-oil presentation usually mid-December (2026 date not announced)

groups.title: On the plate

items.name: Suquet de Peix days in Roses: 16-25 October
items.teaser: Thirteen Roses restaurants put the fishermen's stew on set menus, 30-70 EUR, until Sunday 25 October
items.story: The suquet is the Costa Brava fishermen's stew: rock fish and potato in a sofregit, thickened at the end with a picada of garlic, nuts and saffron. The Ajuntament de Roses gives it ten days each autumn, and in 2026 the Jornades Gastronòmiques del Suquet de Peix run from 16 to 25 October, menus from 30 to 70 EUR. Thirteen restaurants take part, among them El Trull, Rafa's, Cal Negre, Bitakora and L'Àncora. The dates move: the 2025 edition ran 24 October to 2 November. This week is the last chance.
items.why: Book a weekend lunch now; set menus at the small houses fill with locals.
facts: Rafa's is on the list: call ahead, it seats only a handful

items.name: Castanyada and Tots Sants: 31 Oct-1 Nov
items.teaser: Roasted chestnuts, sweet potatoes and pine-nut panellets on All Saints' eve; 1 November is a holiday
items.story: On the night before Tots Sants, Catalonia eats the castanyada: roasted chestnuts, roasted sweet potatoes and panellets, little balls of almond paste rolled in pine nuts, with a glass of sweet wine. Street chestnut stalls appear in the last week of October. One story ties the custom to bell-ringers fed through All Saints' night; another sees panellets as old offerings for the dead. In Girona it falls inside the Fires de Sant Narcís, and the fair's fireworks go up on the evening of 1 November, itself a public holiday.
items.why: Buy panellets from a village pastry shop and serve them with Garnatxa de l'Empordà.

items.name: The calçot season opens
items.teaser: The first calçots arrive in November; Valls marks the start with Calçofest on Saturday 21 November
items.story: Calçots, the long sweet onions charred over vine cuttings, peeled by hand and dragged through romesco, are a November-to-April food; the IGP Calçot de Valls season runs those months. The town of Valls, inland from Tarragona and well south of the Costa Brava, opens the season with the second Calçofest on Saturday 21 November 2026, a day of street shows, a popular calçotada and concerts. Up here the Empordà berenadors and country restaurants put calçotades on the menu as the season builds; the peak is January to March.
items.why: Wait for December for a full calçotada; in November ask for a starter portion.
facts: From November; Calçofest Sat 21 Nov 2026 in Valls

groups.title: In the calendar
groups.desc: Clocks back on Sunday, Girona's stars in play in Huesca on 24 November, and the early-autumn fairs already behind us.

items.name: Clocks go back: Sunday 25 October
items.teaser: Summer time ends at 3:00 on Sunday 25 October: an earlier sunset for every boat and kitchen
items.story: Spain follows the EU rule of ending summer time on the last Sunday of October; in 2026 that is Sunday 25 October, when 3:00 becomes 2:00. It lands in the middle of Girona's fair weekend, the morning of the castellers. On the water it shortens the usable afternoon: tender runs to the coves and the camí de ronda walks between Calella and Llafranc need to start earlier to finish in daylight, and dinner on deck moves into the dark.
items.why: Move the long lunch forward and keep afternoon outings short.
facts: Check that the bridge and crew devices changed

items.name: MICHELIN Spain 2027 gala: Tuesday 24 November
items.teaser: The 2027 stars are announced in Huesca on 24 November: watch the Girona tables
items.story: The ceremony for the MICHELIN Guide Spain 2027 takes place on Tuesday 24 November 2026 at the Palacio de Congresos de Huesca, in the Auditorio Carlos Saura, the first time the gala goes to Aragon, after Málaga. Carmelo Bosque of the one-star Lillas Pastia cooks the dinner. For this coast the evening is about the Girona tables: the three stars of El Celler de Can Roca, the two of Bo.TiC and the one of Els Tinars, and any new name. Results are published the same night.
items.why: Hold bookings at the starred houses before the gala; a new star fills a book overnight.

items.name: Just missed: Begur, L'Escala and Pals
items.teaser: The Fira d'Indians, the anchovy feast and the Pals rice fair are all over for 2026
items.story: Three of the coast's early-autumn dates have passed. Begur's 21st Fira d'Indians, the Cuban-music fair for the town's returned emigrants, ran 4 to 6 September. Pals held its Fira de l'Arròs on Saturday 19 September. L'Escala's 36th Festa de l'Anxova fell on Sunday 4 October, with the tapa route in the bars from 2 to 11 October at 3 EUR a tapa. What remains is the produce: Pals rice in the shops and the salt anchovies of L'Escala, filleted by hand and sold all year at the salting houses.

groups.title: Winter: the urchin and the calçot
groups.desc: The cold months are the coast's table season: urchins in Palafrugell, calçots across Catalonia and the new oil in the Empordà villages.

items.name: La Garoinada of Palafrugell
items.teaser: Palafrugell's winter urchin campaign, since 1992: usually mid-January to late March
items.story: Since 1992 Palafrugell and its sea villages, Calella, Llafranc and Tamariu, have built a winter campaign around the garoina, the violet urchin, eaten when its roe is fullest. In 2026 La Garoinada ran from 16 January to 29 March with nine restaurants and six hotels; in 2025 it was 17 January to 31 March with ten restaurants and four hotels. The end date moves with Holy Week. The urchin comes raw on the half-shell with toasted bread, or worked into eggs and rice.
items.why: Eat the first dozen raw, with bread and nothing else.
facts: Usually mid-January to late March; 2027 dates not yet published

items.name: The calçotada season
items.teaser: Charred onions and romesco, November to April; the great festa in Valls is usually the last Sunday of January
items.story: The calçot season runs from November to April, with its peak from late January. In the Empordà it means long Sunday lunches at country restaurants and berenadors: calçots blackened over vine cuttings, peeled and dipped in romesco, then grilled meat and botifarra with red wine. The reference date is Valls, where the Gran Festa de la Calçotada is held on the last Sunday of January; in 2026 it fell on 25 January. Calçofest in Valls opens the season in late November.
items.why: Book an outdoor calçotada for a still, sunny day; tramuntana ruins it.
facts: November to April; Gran Festa de la Calçotada usually last Sunday of January (25 Jan 2026)

items.teaser: The Alt Empordà's first fair of the year: the new oil in Espolla, usually the third weekend of January
items.story: Espolla, in the vineyards and olive groves under the Albera, holds the first fair of the year in the Alt Empordà, devoted to the new oil and the olive tree. The 29th edition ran on 17 and 18 January 2026 with more than 90 exhibitors; the 2025 fair was 18 and 19 January and the 2024 one 20 and 21 January. It is organised by La Fraternal Espollenca and the Ajuntament, and entry is free. Expect oil tastings, local producers and a village day out.

items.name: Menú and Fira de la Gamba, Palamós
items.teaser: Certified Palamós restaurants serve a gamba menu from late May; the fair fills the fish market in June
items.story: Each late spring Palamós gives its red prawn a campaign. In 2026 the Menú de la Gamba ran from 25 May to 14 June in eight restaurants certified under the Marca de Garantia Gamba de Palamós, and the 11th Fira de la Gamba took over the fish market on the port on Saturday 13 June, from 12:00 to 22:00, with auction tours and cooking demonstrations and free entry. The prawn itself is trawled from the canyon offshore and sold at the afternoon auction on the quay.
items.why: Do the fair's auction tour, then order the prawn simply grilled at a certified house.

items.teaser: Girona's old town dressed in flower installations for nine days in May
items.story: For nine days each May, Girona fills its courtyards, stairways and churches with floral installations, and the Barri Vell opens patios that are closed the rest of the year. The 2026 edition ran from 9 to 17 May, with 141 floral projects in 113 locations around the city. Early mornings and weekdays are calmer than the weekends. It pairs well with a market morning at the Mercat del Lleó.

items.name: Pals i la Cuina de l'Arròs
items.teaser: Pals rice on restaurant menus from mid-April to the end of May; a rice fair follows in September
items.story: Rice has grown in the Empordà wetlands below Pals since the fifteenth century, and the town gives it a spring campaign. The 33rd Pals i la Cuina de l'Arròs ran from 15 April to 31 May 2026, with the local restaurants cooking rice dishes from the town's paddies. A separate Fira de l'Arròs de Pals is held in late summer: in 2026 on Saturday 19 September at the Pati de Ca la Pruna, with tastings of at least five varieties. Buy the rice in the village to take aboard.
items.why: Order the arròs of the day and buy a bag of the same rice to cook on board.

items.name: Fira d'Indians, Begur
items.teaser: Begur's fair for its Cuba-rich emigrants: Cuban music and rum, usually the first weekend of September
items.story: In the nineteenth century men from Begur went to Cuba, made money and came home to build the colonial mansions that still stand in the old town. The Fira d'Indians remembers them. The 21st edition ran from 4 to 6 September 2026, with a Caribbean-style market, old trades, street shows, Cuban bands, guided visits and tastings of coffee, rum and chocolate across the Plaça Forgas and the Parc de l'Arbreda. Most activities are free. In 2025 it ran 5 to 7 September.
items.why: Wear white and walk the Indiano mansions before the evening concerts.
facts: Usually the first weekend of September (4-6 Sep 2026); 2027 not yet published

items.name: Festa de l'Anxova, L'Escala
items.teaser: L'Escala's day for its salt anchovy, usually the first Sunday of October, with a tapa route in the bars
items.story: L'Escala has salted anchovies for centuries and gives them a festa at the start of October. The 36th edition fell on Sunday 4 October 2026: the pregó and the Anxova d'Or presented at noon at La Punta, a popular tasting on La Riba and havaneres by Oreig de Mar at 12:30. Around it, the Ruta de la Tapa de l'Anxova ran from 2 to 11 October, at 3 EUR a tapa, with a stamp passport for prize draws. The 2025 edition was the first weekend of October too.
